 Follow Scarlett Johansson Makes Candid Admission About Being In Charge In Her Marriage With ‘SNL’ Star Colin Jost
 Favour Adegoke Updated Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:00 PM UTC 5 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Scarlett Johansson Makes Candid Admission About Being In Charge In Her Marriage With ‘SNL’ Star Colin Jost Scarlett Johansson has offered a glimpse into her marriage to Colin Jost , revealing that she considers herself the person in charge of their household.
 The actress also opened up about motherhood, explaining how she and the comedian coordinate their demanding careers to give their children as normal a childhood as possible.
 Despite her celebrity status, Scarlett Johansson says protecting her family's privacy remains one of her biggest priorities.
 Scarlett Johansson Calls Herself The 'CEO' Of Her Household 
 Ron Sachs – CNP / MEGA
 Johansson is not shy about acknowledging her leadership role at home with Jost. During an interview with the Los Angeles Times on Wednesday, November 11, the actress described herself as the person who oversees their household.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I consider myself the CEO of our household," She said. Johansson, who shares five-year-old son Cosmo with the "Saturday Night Live" comedian, added that being a mother remains one of the most important parts of her life.
 "I'm a hands-on parent. I love being a mom," she explained. "Kids have so much going on, and their lives are important."
 Johansson also revealed that she and Jost make a conscious effort to coordinate their schedules to ensure their children's routines remain as normal as possible, despite their parents' high-profile careers.
 The couple, who married in October 2020, are also raising Johansson's 12-year-old daughter, Rose, whom she shares with her former husband, French journalist Romain Dauriac.
 The Actress Has Explained Why She Keeps Her Children's Lives Private 
 MEGA
 Johansson has long been protective of Rose and Cosmo, making a conscious decision to keep them largely out of the public eye.
 Advertisement Advertisement During an interview with InStyle last year, she explained that privacy was particularly important when it came to her children and their ability to grow up without the pressures of celebrity culture.
 "My family is very precious to me, as is their privacy," she said, adding that "the anonymity of my children is very precious to me."
 The actress also explained that she does not want her children to feel that they have to live under the spotlight simply because their parents are famous.
 "I think preserving that for as long as possible until it's someone's choice, that's the choice I make as far as my kids go," she said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Johansson has spent much of her life in the entertainment industry, having started acting as a child before becoming one of Hollywood's most recognizable stars. Her experiences have seemingly influenced her determination to give Rose and Cosmo as ordinary an upbringing as possible.
 Scarlett Johansson said she no longer gets cast for her "desirability" or the male gaze.

 The actress said no man had ever asked her out "traditionally" before Colin Jost.
 Driver and Johansson had "some very intimate" moments on "Marriage Story" .
 Johansson called out an unruly photographer for not being "respectful." 
 Johansson admits she felt "faint" hearing Jost's "gross" "SNL" joke about her.
 Scarlett Johansson Once Admitted She Panicked During Her First Date With Colin Jost 
 MEGA
 Johansson previously admitted that she panicked during her first proper date with Jost, despite enjoying their dinner at an Italian restaurant in New York's East Village, per E-News .
 "I was a serial monogamist, and I never got the sort of traditional like, 'Hey, would you like to have dinner sometime?'" she recalled.
 Advertisement Advertisement After dinner, Jost suggested they meet some friends for a drink, but Johansson became flustered and decided to head home instead.
 "I hadn't dated basically ever, so I was just like, 'I have to go now.' I need to leave," she explained.
 She later revealed that Jost thought her abrupt departure meant she was no longer interested. "Later he was like, 'I totally thought that was it. You were acting so weird.' I panicked. I don't know," she said.
 Despite the awkward start, their romance eventually blossomed. The pair first met in 2006 when Johansson hosted Saturday Night Live, began dating years later, got engaged in 2019, and married in October 2020.
 Colin Jost Has Also Shared His First Impression Of His Famous Wife 
 MEGA
 Jost has previously offered his own perspective on their early connection, revealing that he was impressed by Johansson long before they became a couple, as reported by US Weekly .
 Advertisement Advertisement In his 2020 memoir, "A Very Punchable Face", the comedian recalled meeting the actress when she hosted "Saturday Night Live" in 2006.
 He described her as "beautiful, smart, sweet and intimidatingly sophisticated", while joking that he felt considerably less impressive by comparison.
 Jost also admitted that he had been struck by the difference in their confidence and maturity at the time, particularly given Johansson's already established career.
 Years later, their relationship became one of Hollywood's more closely followed romances, although both have generally avoided sharing too many intimate details about their marriage.
 Scarlett Johansson's Family Is Supporting Her Latest Hollywood Projects 
 MEGA
 Away from her responsibilities at home, Johansson is continuing to expand her work across film and entertainment.
 Advertisement Advertisement In an interview with People Magazine published on November 12, the actress discussed her return to singing for Netflix's upcoming animated film "Ray Gunn", revealing that her family has been supportive of the project.
 Johansson voices pop star Venus Nova in the Brad Bird-directed film and performs five songs, marking her first on-screen singing role since "Sing 2" in 2021.
 The actress revealed that her daughter Rose's encouragement has been particularly meaningful, while Jost has also supported her return to music.
 She added, "I'm very lucky," expressing gratitude for her family's support before noting, "We all boost each other up as much as we can."
 Advertisement Advertisement The film, which also features the voices of Sam Rockwell and Tom Waits, is scheduled to arrive in select cinemas on December 4 before making its Netflix debut on December 18.
 Johansson has also been busy with several other projects, including James Gray's crime thriller "Paper Tiger" and an upcoming film from director Ari Aster.
